subject.title: fix(tts): defer text settlement for final-mode TTS to eliminate churn (#83511)

question: Should OpenClaw expose `captionedFinalText` as a public channel capability and enable that delivery behavior by default for Telegram final-mode TTS?
rationale: The capability is extension-facing and changes when core suppresses visible text, so code correctness alone cannot determine whether this should become a supported plugin contract and Telegram default.

options.title: Accept capability with proof
options.body: Approve the generic capability and Telegram opt-in, then require redacted exact-head Telegram proof across the changed delivery and recovery scenarios before merge.

options.title: Keep the seam internal
options.body: Replace the public capability with a narrower bundled-Telegram seam and defer an external plugin contract until more channels need it.

options.title: Pause the direction
options.body: Keep existing separate text and voice delivery until maintainers choose a broader TTS delivery policy, potentially alongside https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/issues/42539.

recommendation.title: Accept capability with proof
recommendation.body: Approve the generic capability and Telegram opt-in, then require redacted exact-head Telegram proof across the changed delivery and recovery scenarios before merge.

likelyOwner.reason: The feature history spans core dispatch and plugin capability policy, and this owner has repeated relevant changes across both boundaries.
